verses.text: Then David said, “This is the house of Yahweh God, and this is the altar of burnt offering for Israel.”
David gave orders to gather together the foreigners who were in the land of Israel; and he set masons to cut dressed stones to build God’s house.
David prepared iron in abundance for the nails for the doors of the gates, and for the couplings; and brass in abundance without weight;
and cedar trees without number, for the Sidonians and the people of Tyre brought cedar trees in abundance to David.

David said, “Solomon my son is young and tender, and the house that is to be built for Yahweh must be exceedingly magnificent, of fame and of glory throughout all countries. I will therefore make preparation for it.” So David prepared abundantly before his death.
Then he called for Solomon his son, and commanded him to build a house for Yahweh, the God of Israel.
David said to Solomon his son, “As for me, it was in my heart to build a house to the name of Yahweh my God.
But Yahweh’s word came to me, saying, ‘You have shed blood abundantly, and have made great wars. You shall not build a house to my name, because you have shed much blood on the earth in my sight.

Behold, a son shall be born to you, who shall be a man of peace. I will give him rest from all his enemies all around; for his name shall be Solomon, and I will give peace and quietness to Israel in his days.
He shall build a house for my name; and he will be my son, and I will be his father; and I will establish the throne of his kingdom over Israel for ever.’
Now, my son, may Yahweh be with you and prosper you, and build the house of Yahweh your God, as he has spoken concerning you.
May Yahweh give you discretion and understanding, and put you in charge of Israel; that so you may keep the law of Yahweh your God.
Then you will prosper, if you observe to do the statutes and the ordinances which Yahweh gave Moses concerning Israel. Be strong and courageous. Don’t be afraid, and don’t be dismayed.

Now, behold, in my affliction I have prepared for Yahweh’s house one hundred thousand talents  of gold, one million talents  of silver, and brass and iron without weight; for it is in abundance. I have also prepared timber and stone; and you may add to them.
There are also workmen with you in abundance, cutters and workers of stone and timber, and all kinds of men who are skillful in every kind of work;
of the gold, the silver, the brass, and the iron, there is no number. Arise and be doing, and may Yahweh be with you.”
David also commanded all the princes of Israel to help Solomon his son, saying,
“Isn’t Yahweh your God with you? Hasn’t he given you rest on every side? For he has delivered the inhabitants of the land into my hand; and the land is subdued before Yahweh, and before his people.

Now set your heart and your soul to follow Yahweh your God. Arise therefore, and build the sanctuary of Yahweh God, to bring the ark of Yahweh’s covenant and the holy vessels of God into the house that is to be built for Yahweh’s name.”

footnotes.content: David has claimed the threshing floor of Araunah as God's dwelling place. After all the years of wandering—the tent, the carrying—he's finally found stillness for the Ark. There's a deep tenderness in how he points to this place: 'This is it.' Sometimes the Lord brings us to our threshold after a long road.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: David doesn't build alone; he gathers the foreigners living among Israel. The work of God's house includes the outsider, the immigrant, the one without tribal claim. They become stonemasons, cutters of the foundation. I've learned that God often builds his kingdom through unexpected hands.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Iron for the nails, brass without measure—David is preparing the raw stuff of construction. The detail is striking: he doesn't just dream of a house, he stockpiles iron and metal in 'abundance.' There's a lesson in that for any calling the Lord sets before us: start with the simple preparation that's truly yours to do.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The Sidonians and Tyrians send cedar trees in abundance. Even those who don't worship Yahweh are drawn to give for His house. I've seen the same in my time: when work is truly for the Lord's glory, provision comes from quarters we never expected, often from those who simply respect what's excellent and true.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Here is David's heart laid bare: Solomon is young and untested, yet David prepares abundantly anyway. He knows his role is not to build, but to ready the way for the one who will. It's a beautiful image of a parent who loves enough to work for their child's future, not their own glory.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: David calls Solomon and charges him: 'Build this house for Yahweh, God of Israel.' The word passed from father to son carries weight. I think of all the faithful charges that have traveled down through generations—a mother's prayer, a grandfather's steady faith—and how they shape the one who receives them.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: David confesses his own desire: 'It was in my heart to build.' He wanted this for himself, yet the Lord set a different path. There's no bitterness here, only honesty. Sometimes the deepest peace comes when we name what we longed for, then release it to the one who knows better.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: The reason lands hard: 'You have shed blood abundantly.' David was a warrior first, and that calling was real and necessary—yet it disqualified him from building God's house. Our gifts and our seasons are often different. The same hands that fight cannot always construct. That's not failure; it's order.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: A son shall be born—Solomon, the man of peace. God names him before his birth, names him by his calling: peace and quietness in his days. How tenderly the Lord prepares his vessels. Before Solomon ever drew breath, his purpose was woven in.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Solomon will build the house, and God promises him a father's love—'I will be his father.' The Almighty claims him as son, and pledges that his kingdom shall endure forever. What a threshold for a young man: his work matters, his future is secure, and he is loved with a love deeper than any earthly father's.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: David's prayer for his son: 'May Yahweh be with you and prosper you.' He doesn't bless Solomon with wealth or ease, but with presence and purpose. The greatest inheritance a father can leave is not silver but a living God at his son's side.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: David asks not for Solomon's pleasure but for his wisdom—'discretion and understanding.' He prays that his son will keep the law, will lead with judgment. A parent who prays for their child's character over their comfort has learned something true.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: 'Be strong and courageous. Don't be afraid.' The charge rings clear across centuries. Solomon will need courage, not for battle like his father, but for faithfulness—to keep the statutes, to stand firm. The Lord calls young men to strength in the same way in every age.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: A hundred thousand talents of gold, a million talents of silver—the numbers are almost beyond reckoning. David has stockpiled more treasure than most nations command, prepared it 'in my affliction.' What he could not build with his own hands, he has prepared with his wealth and foresight. That is a father's love made tangible.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: David surrounds Solomon with skilled workmen—'cutters and workers of stone and timber, all kinds of men who are skillful.' He knows his son cannot do this alone. Wisdom is sometimes simply this: gathering the right people, the capable hands, and setting them to work together.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: 'Arise and be doing, and may Yahweh be with you.' The instruction is simple: start. Don't wait for perfect clarity or endless preparation. The gold, silver, brass, and iron are ready. The workers are assembled. The command is to move. I've found the Lord often blesses action taken in faith more than endless deliberation.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: David calls the princes of Israel to aid his son. He doesn't leave Solomon to lead in isolation. Authority shared is authority strengthened. The older men, those with experience, are commanded to stand with the young king. There's wisdom in that order.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: 'Isn't Yahweh your God with you?' David reminds Israel's princes of the foundation: their God is present and has given them rest on every side. The enemies are subdued. The land is at peace. Now, from that place of rest and security, they are called to build. Peace is the soil where God's work takes root.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight

footnotes.content: Readers today hear an echo of this charge: 'Set your heart and soul to follow Yahweh your God.' In our own time of many tasks and pulled allegiances, that old word still calls us to a singular focus—to build, yes, but first to follow. The work follows the heart.
footnotes.author: LLT Insight
